encounters.cc: Difficulty with night driving and occasionally bumping into objects at the periphery of vision during routine follow-up.

lines: Difficulty with night driving and occasionally bumping into objects at the periphery of vision during routine follow-up.
He mentions that he has been experiencing difficulty with night driving and occasionally bumps into objects at the periphery of his vision.
He denies any eye pain or redness.
- Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3 secondary to diabetic nephropathy
His medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with hydrochlorothiazide, and type 2 diabetes mellitus, managed with metformin.
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement
- Latanoprost 1 drop in both eyes at bedtime
His family history is notable for a brother with glaucoma.
Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine per week).
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
On physical examination, visual acuity is 20/25 in both eyes.
Intraocular pressure measures 22 mmHg in the right eye and 24 mmHg in the left eye.
Fundoscopic examination reveals an increased cup-to-disc ratio of 0.7 in both eyes.
Visual field testing shows bilateral peripheral vision loss.

lines: Concern about a new slowly growing lesion on his back that he first noticed several months ago, denying pain or bleeding.

He first noticed the lesion several months ago, and it has slowly increased in size.
He denies any pain, itching, or bleeding from the lesion.
- Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3 secondary to diabetic nephropathy
His medical history is significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement
- Latanoprost 1 drop in both eyes at bedtime
- Mother: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma

Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
He denies any recent weight loss, fever, or night sweats
On physical examination, you note a well-demarcated, round, tan lesion with a "stuck-on" appearance on his upper back.
The lesion measures 1.5 cm in diameter and has a slightly rough surface.
No other similar lesions are noted on full skin examination.

encounters.cc: Progressive nausea, vomiting, early satiety, and 10-pound weight loss over 3 months with unusually high blood glucose levels.

lines: Progressive nausea, vomiting, early satiety, and 10-pound weight loss over 3 months with unusually high blood glucose levels.

This 69-year-old male with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3, and Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma, with established care in Ophthalmology, Dermatology, and Internal Medicine, presents to Gastroenterology with a 3-month history of progressive nausea, vomiting, early satiety, and a 10-pound weight loss.
He reports that the vomiting occurs after meals and consists of undigested food.
However, he notes that his blood glucose levels have been unusually high in the past few weeks despite no changes in diet or medication.
- Chronic Kidney Disease due to Diabetic Nephropathy (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3 secondary to diabetic nephropathy
His past medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, which has been well-controlled with metformin.
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement
- Latanoprost 1 drop in both eyes at bedtime
- Mother: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine per week).
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
Physical examination reveals mild epigastric tenderness and a palpable mass in the upper abdomen.
An upper gastrointestinal series demonstrates delayed gastric emptying and a narrowing at the distal stomach.

encounters.cc: Two-month history of itchy red patches progressing to large tense blisters over abdomen, arms, and thighs.

lines: Two-month history of itchy red patches progressing to large tense blisters over abdomen, arms, and thighs.
This 70-year-old male with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, pancreatic carcinoma, and prior dermatology evaluation for melanocytic nevi presents with a new skin complaint.
He initially noticed red, raised patches on his trunk that he attributed to an allergic reaction.
Over the past two weeks, he has developed large, tense blisters over his abdomen, arms, and thighs.
He denies any new medications, soaps, or detergents.
- Chronic Kidney Disease due to Diabetic Nephropathy (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3 secondary to diabetic nephropathy
His past medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement
- Latanoprost 1 drop in both eyes at bedtime
- Mother: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine per week).
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
On physical examination, you note multiple 1-3 cm tense bullae on an erythematous base, some with surrounding urticarial plaques.
A skin biopsy is performed, and direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposition along the basement membrane zone.

encounters.cc: Three days of worsening constant dull left lower quadrant abdominal pain with low-grade fever, nausea, and decreased appetite.

lines: Three days of worsening constant dull left lower quadrant abdominal pain with low-grade fever, nausea, and decreased appetite.
This 71-year-old male with a history of pancreatic carcinoma diagnosed in 2021 and chronic kidney disease stage 3 secondary to diabetic nephropathy presents with abdominal pain.
He describes the pain as a constant, dull ache localized to the lower left quadrant of his abdomen.
He also reports decreased appetite, nausea, and occasional loose stools over the past 2 days.
He denies vomiting, hematochezia, or melena.
He has had similar, less intense episodes in the past that resolved without treatment, but this time the pain has been more severe and persistent.
- Chronic Kidney Disease due to Diabetic Nephropathy (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3 secondary to diabetic nephropathy
His medical history includes type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension.
He had a normal colonoscopy 5 years ago.
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement
- Latanoprost 1 drop in both eyes at bedtime
- Mother: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
He does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally.
On exam, his temperature is 38.2°C (100.8°F), blood pressure is 128/74 mmHg, and pulse is 94/min.
Abdominal exam reveals tenderness to palpation in the left lower quadrant without rebound or guarding.
Laboratory studies show leukocytosis. A urinalysis is negative for infection or hematuria.
An abdominal CT scan with contrast demonstrates pericolic fat stranding and localized bowel wall thickening of the sigmoid colon without abscess or free air.

encounters.cc: Acute onset of chest pain radiating to left arm associated with shortness of breath and diaphoresis starting 2 hours ago.

lines: Acute onset of chest pain radiating to left arm associated with shortness of breath and diaphoresis starting 2 hours ago.
This 72-year-old male with diabetes and CKD presents with chest pain.
The pain started 2 hours ago and is associated with shortness of breath and diaphoresis.
- Chronic Kidney Disease due to Diabetic Nephropathy (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3 secondary to diabetic nephropathy
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement
His current medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Latanoprost 1 drop in both eyes at bedtime
- Mother: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine per week).
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
On examination, his blood pressure is 160/90 mmHg, heart rate is 102 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute.
His baseline serum creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) is 40 mL/min/1.73m^2.
An electrocardiogram shows ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF.
The patient is diagnosed with an ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)
He is scheduled for an urgent coronary angiography.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of severe dyspnea and productive cough with pink, frothy sputum while watching television at home.

lines: Sudden onset of severe dyspnea and productive cough with pink, frothy sputum while watching television at home.
This 73-year-old male with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3, and prior contrast-induced nephropathy presents to the Emergency Department.
He reports that his symptoms began suddenly while he was watching television.
- Chronic Kidney Disease due to Diabetic Nephropathy (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3 secondary to diabetic nephropathy
- Cardiac catheterization with drug-eluting stent placement
- Latanoprost 1 drop in both eyes at bedtime
- Mother: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma
Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 glasses of wine per week).
Occupation: Retired high school mathematics teacher.
On examination, he is tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 30 breaths per minute, blood pressure is 180/100 mmHg, heart rate is 110 beats per minute, and oxygen saturation is 85% on room air.
Auscultation of the lungs reveals bilateral rales halfway up both lung fields.
The patient's jugular venous pressure is elevated, and there is 2+ pitting edema in both lower extremities.
The patient's serum creatinine is 1.2 mg/dL, and B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) is significantly elevated.
Chest X-ray demonstrates pulmonary edema with cephalization of blood flow and Kerley B lines.
An electrocardiogram shows ST-segment elevations in leads II, III, and aVF.
